_comment: Curated topics from the competitor content gap analysis (docs/competitor-content-gaps.md, 2026-08-25). Queued into ContentEngine by scripts/content-engine/add-gap-topics.js. Each was checked against published coverage before being added; two shortlist against existing posts on generic tokens and will be adjudicated by the duplicate guard in publish-blog.js, which is correct. Add new topics here rather than editing the script.
_source: Sitemap analysis of Together, MT Finance, West One, Roma Finance, Octane Capital (7 topics), plus leasehold gaps found 2026-08-26 when a freeholder-insolvency news story had no relevant bridging article to link to (4 topics)

topics.title: HMO Licensing Rules And How They Affect Your Finance Options
topics.brief: Competitor gap: West One and Together both cover HMOs; Boxx has only bridging-loans-for-hmo-conversion. Explain mandatory vs additional vs selective licensing, what triggers each, and — the part lenders care about — how licensing status changes what finance is available and when. Cover the practical sequencing problem: licences often cannot be granted until works complete, but lenders want to see the route to one. Explain how bridging covers that window and what the exit looks like.

topics.title: How HMO Commercial Valuation Changes What You Can Borrow
topics.brief: Zero Boxx coverage. Explain the difference between bricks-and-mortar valuation and commercial/investment valuation on an HMO, why a converted HMO can be worth substantially more on a yield basis, and how that changes loan size on both the bridge and the exit. Use worked arithmetic with realistic UK figures. Be explicit that not every lender applies commercial valuation and what determines whether they will.

topics.title: Refinancing An HMO Onto A Term Mortgage After Conversion
topics.brief: The exit half of the HMO story, which Boxx's existing conversion post does not cover. Walk through the refinance route once works complete and the property is let: what lenders require (licence, tenancy setup, letting history), typical timescales, and how to avoid the bridge running out before the term lender is ready. Emphasise planning the exit before drawing the bridge.

topics.title: Student HMO Property: What Landlords Need To Know About Funding
topics.brief: Both West One and Together publish on student accommodation; Boxx has nothing. Cover what makes student HMOs different for a lender — academic-year void periods, joint and several tenancies, guarantors, purpose-built competition — and how that affects both bridging and the term exit. Practical, not promotional.

topics.title: Raising Business Capital Against A Rental Property You Already Own
topics.keyword: second charge rental property business capital
topics.brief: Competitor gap: West One covers second charges for business purposes; Boxx has product explainers but not the use case. Explain raising capital against existing rental equity without disturbing a good first-charge rate, when a second charge beats a remortgage, and the regulatory distinction around business-purpose lending. Show the arithmetic comparing remortgage vs second charge over a realistic term.

topics.title: Using A Second Charge Loan To Fund EPC Upgrades On A Rental
topics.brief: Ties the second-charge gap to the EPC pressure landlords are already reading about. Cover typical upgrade costs, why many landlords will not want to disturb a low fixed first charge, and how a second charge funds the work. Be accurate and hedged about the current state of MEES requirements rather than stating a deadline as settled fact.

topics.title: Top Slicing Explained: Personal Income And Buy-To-Let Affordability
topics.keyword: top slicing buy to let affordability
topics.brief: Together covers this; Boxx has zero coverage. Explain what top slicing is, when a lender will let surplus personal income cover a rental shortfall, which borrower profiles it suits, and its limits. A genuine question landlords ask that the site currently cannot answer.

topics.title: Bridging Finance For Buying Your Freehold: How Collective Enfranchisement Is Funded
topics.brief: Zero coverage, and a textbook bridging use case. Leaseholders exercising the statutory right to buy their freehold need funds before any refinance is possible. Explain the process and timescales, why participating leaseholders often cannot all raise cash at once, how a bridge covers the gap, and what the exit looks like once the freehold is owned and lease extensions granted. Be accurate and hedged about the Leasehold and Freehold Reform Act rather than stating provisions as settled where they are still being implemented.

topics.title: Funding A Lease Extension Before You Remortgage
topics.brief: Complements short-lease-flat-mortgage-refused, which covers the problem but not this solution. A short lease blocks mainstream lending, but extending needs money up front - the classic chicken-and-egg a bridge solves. Cover the premium, valuation, the 80-year marriage value threshold, and how the post-extension remortgage repays the bridge. Show the arithmetic with realistic figures.

topics.title: Finance Options When Your Flat Is Unsellable Because Of Cladding
topics.brief: Zero coverage of a problem affecting many UK flat owners. Cover why lenders decline, what EWS1 and remediation status change, and the realistic finance routes for someone who needs to move or raise capital meanwhile. Be careful and factual about remediation funding schemes rather than promising outcomes, and do not imply bridging solves an unsellable flat - it buys time, which is a different claim.

topics.title: What Happens To Your Flat If The Freeholder Goes Bust
topics.brief: Prompted by the Spectrum Building case covered in the news section. Explain what freeholder insolvency means for leaseholders - service charges, insurance, remediation liability, and the right of first refusal to buy the freehold. Then the finance angle: how leaseholders fund a collective purchase at short notice. Link to the news article for the real-world example.
